title: Home water safety checklist
intro: Walk through your home and yard with this list. Check off every layer you have, and make a plan for the ones you don’t. No single layer is enough.

sections.title: Supervision
items: We name one adult as the Water Watcher any time kids are in or near water.
The Water Watcher puts the phone away and hands off to another adult every 15 minutes.
Toddlers and weak swimmers stay within arm’s reach.

sections.title: Barriers
items: A fence at least 4 feet tall surrounds the pool on all four sides. The house is not one of the sides.
The gate closes and latches by itself, and we never prop it open.
Chairs, toys and planters are away from the fence so no one can climb it.

sections.title: Alarms
items: Every door and window that opens toward the pool has an alarm.
We have a pool alarm or a wearable wristband alarm.
Alarms stay on, especially when we have guests, and we test them and keep spare batteries.

sections.title: Covers & drains
items: The pool has a certified safety cover (ASTM F1346), and we pump standing water off it.
We empty and flip kiddie pools, buckets and coolers after every use.
Pool and spa drains have anti-entrapment covers, and above-ground pool ladders come out after swimming.
We checked our above-ground pool against the CPSC compression strap recall.

sections.title: Swim skills
items: Our kids are in swim lessons that fit their age (the AAP says many kids can start at age 1).
The adults in our house can swim, too.

sections.title: Life jackets
items: Every child has a U.S. Coast Guard-approved life jacket that fits their weight.
Kids wear them at lakes, rivers and on boats, even on shore.

sections.title: Emergency ready
items: Everyone who watches our kids knows to check the water first if a child is missing.
At least one adult in the house knows infant and child CPR.
A charged phone, a reaching pole and a ring buoy are at the pool.
Our address and emergency numbers are posted near the pool.

sitterIntro: Thank you for watching our kids. Around water, here’s how we do it:
sitterItems: If a child is missing, check the water first: pool, hot tub, bathtub, buckets. Then call 911.
When kids are in or near water, you’re the Water Watcher. Phone away, eyes on the water.
Toddlers stay within arm’s reach, in the pool and in the bath.
The pool gate stays closed and the alarms stay on. Please don’t prop doors open.
Empty buckets and kiddie pools when you’re done.
